newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound dips sharply against stg/mark.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound dips sharply against stg/mark.

text.p: The Irish pound tumbled against sterling, the mark and dollar on heavy foreign selling when markets opened on Wednesday, dealers said.
It fell around two pence against sterling, lost three cents against the dollar and was quoted almost five pfennigs down against the mark.
Dealers said the sharp fall was a continuation of a trend set earlier this week which caused Central Bank intervention to prop up the Irish pound.
They said the market was convinced that the Irish currency would have to fall because of the country's near certain membership of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"There is absolutely no doubt about our EMU membership," said one dealer.
"But the market believes that it would be unrealistic for the Irish currency to join at its current levels. It has to fall and a rate of 90 pence sterling is not impossible," the dealer said.
The punt was quoted at 92.85 pence, 2.6225 marks and $1.5185 from a close on Tuesday at 0.9485 sterling, 2.6705 marks and $1.5481.

"The perception in the market was that the Central Bank was holding the Irish pound at a level that could not be sustained. We have seen a lot of continued overseas selling as a result," another dealer said.
"If Ireland is to join EMU, it will have to be a mid-rate of 2.40 to 2.41 against the mark and not as high as it had been," the dealer said.
Dealers said the Irish pound remained near the top of the ERM grid 8.96 percent above the weakest currency, the French franc, compared with 11.37 percent above the same unit on Tuesday.
They said the market was still digesting the importance of remarks by Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn in a Reuters television interview last week.
The minister said he was "somewhat concerned" at the strength of the Irish pound in the ERM grid and that he would prefer it to closer to its median point.
Money market rates have risen briskly in response to the punt's weakness. One-month rates were quoted at 6.0/0.25 pct by 0840 GMT, against 5.81/5.94 at Tuesday's close.
Dealers said a 6.0 percent one-month rate was seen as a key level indicating pressure for a rise in retail rates.
